ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Optimality gap versus city count at fixed model capacity
PROPOSAL: Train a 4M-parameter transformer policy on planar Euclidean TSP instances with 20, 40, 80 and 160 cities, supervised by optimal tours from an exact solver and trained until validation loss stops moving, with a learning rate picked on a held-out split. Measure the mean optimality gap on 2000 fresh instances per size and fit a power law and an exponential in the city count. Run 3 seeds. The aim is to isolate how the achievable limit degrades as the solution space grows while the model size stays fixed.
CONTROLS: Nearest-neighbour and farthest-insertion tours as floor references, an 8M-parameter variant at 80 cities to confirm the regime is capacity limited, and a doubled training length at 160 cities to confirm the plateau.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: The gap should rise smoothly and roughly as a power law in the city count. It could fail if the 160-city runs have not reached their plateau, which would bend the fit upward.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Optimality gap for a routing transformer at three city counts
PROPOSAL: Train a 24M-parameter transformer policy on planar Euclidean TSP instances with 20, 50 and 100 cities, supervised by optimal tours from an exact solver and trained to convergence under two decay schedules. Evaluate the optimality gap on 1000 fresh instances with greedy decoding, sampling and beam search, and fit a power law in the city count. Run 8 seeds and keep the best checkpoint by validation gap. This shows how the limit degrades with the solution space at a fixed model size.
CONTROLS: Nearest-neighbour and farthest-insertion tours as floor references, a 2-opt refinement applied to the network tours, and a comparison of the two schedules at 50 cities to confirm they reach the same plateau.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: The gap should rise smoothly with the city count, with the decoding strategy shifting the level but not the trend. It could fail if the schedules settle at different levels, so that the fitted exponent depends on the schedule.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gap growth as point dimension rises at fixed city count
PROPOSAL: Generate TSP instances with 50 cities whose coordinates lie in 2, 4, 8 and 16 dimensions, sampled uniformly in the unit cube, and train a 3M-parameter transformer to imitate solver tours until validation loss is flat. Report the optimality gap and fit its dependence on dimension. Use 5 seeds. The aim is to see how performance degrades as the representation grows and distances concentrate.
CONTROLS: Nearest-neighbour tours as a floor reference, a model of the same capacity trained on 2-dimensional instances to anchor the scale, and a check that the exact-solver tour length follows the known scaling in the unit cube.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The gap should grow with dimension and flatten once distances concentrate. It could fail if the 16-dimensional runs under-train, in which case the apparent growth reflects optimisation rather than capacity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gap behaviour of a routing network on three planar instance families
PROPOSAL: Generate TSP instances with 50 cities in 2 dimensions drawn from uniform, clustered and ring-shaped distributions, and train a 16M-parameter transformer to imitate solver tours until validation loss is flat. Report the optimality gap on 1000 fresh instances together with the entropy of the attention weights at 5 checkpoints, and fit the gap as a function of training step. Use 3 seeds. The aim is to see whether the geometry of the instance family moves the limit.
CONTROLS: Nearest-neighbour tours as a floor reference, an 8M-parameter model trained on the uniform family to anchor the scale, and a check that the exact-solver tour length follows the known planar scaling.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The gap should be similar for the three families while attention entropy falls as training proceeds. It could fail if the clustered family sits clearly apart, in which case that family would need its own trend.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Imitation versus policy-gradient training at fixed capacity
PROPOSAL: Train a 6M-parameter transformer on 100-city planar TSP under three regimes: imitation of exact tours, REINFORCE with a shared baseline, and REINFORCE initialised from the imitation weights, all run until the validation gap stops improving. Evaluate the optimality gap on 1000 fresh instances after sampling 16 tours per instance. Use 3 seeds. This tests whether the achievable limit depends on how the model is trained or only on its capacity.
CONTROLS: A 12M-parameter imitation model to separate the effect of capacity from the effect of the training signal, a random-insertion floor, and a policy-gradient run with doubled training length to confirm convergence.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Imitation should reach a lower gap than policy gradient from scratch, with the warm-started run in the middle. It could fail if the policy-gradient runs simply have not converged, which the longer run would reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reinforcement training of a routing transformer with three baselines
PROPOSAL: Train a 48M-parameter transformer on 50-city planar TSP with REINFORCE using a shared baseline, a greedy rollout baseline and a learned critic, running all three until the validation gap stops improving and then continuing for 2 more rounds of training. Evaluate the optimality gap on 1000 fresh instances after sampling 16 tours, and log gradient variance at 8 checkpoints. Use 5 seeds. This shows how much the training signal moves the limit at fixed capacity.
CONTROLS: An imitation-trained model of the same size as a reference, a random-insertion floor, and a run of the learned critic with a halved learning rate to confirm convergence.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: The greedy rollout baseline should give the lowest gap with the shared baseline slightly behind. It could fail if the critic run diverges, in which case the comparison reflects optimisation noise rather than the limit.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Extrapolating gap trends from short to far longer instances
PROPOSAL: Fit a power law to the optimality gap of 5M-parameter transformers trained by imitation at 10, 20, 30 and 40 cities, then predict the gap at 80, 160 and 320 cities and verify by training at those sizes with the same procedure, 8 seeds, with intervals from bootstrap resamples on all fits. Compare the prediction error with that of a log-linear fit. This tests whether trends fitted on a short range still hold far beyond it.
CONTROLS: A constant-gap predictor and a log-linear fit as competing forecasts, a held-out size at 60 cities used to choose the fit form, and a rerun of the 320-city model with doubled training steps to confirm convergence.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The power law should predict the longer sizes within a few points of gap. It could fail if the 320-city model is capacity starved in a way the small sizes did not show, which would bend the trend.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Forecasting gap trends from short ranges with a family of trained networks
PROPOSAL: Fit a power law to the optimality gap of 30M-parameter transformers trained by imitation at 10, 20 and 40 cities, then predict the gap at 80 cities and verify by training a model at that size with 3 seeds, 3 weight decay values and 2 context lengths. Compare the prediction error with that of a log-linear fit and of a Gaussian process fit. The aim is to see whether trends from small sizes survive a jump to bigger ones.
CONTROLS: A constant-gap predictor as the null forecast, a held-out size at 30 cities used to choose among the fit forms, and a rerun at 80 cities with doubled training steps to confirm convergence.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The power law should predict the 80-city gap within a few points. It could fail if the Gaussian process wins on held-out error, in which case the simple form is not supported.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Capacity scaling of the achievable gap at a fixed instance size
PROPOSAL: Train transformers of 0.5M, 1M, 2M, 4M and 8M parameters on 50-city planar TSP by imitation until validation loss stops moving, 3 seeds. Fit the optimality gap as a function of parameter count with a saturating power law and report the estimated irreducible gap. The target is how the limit of achievable performance depends on the size of the model once data and training are not binding.
CONTROLS: The exact-solver length as the lower bound, nearest-neighbour tours as the upper reference, and a refit that drops the smallest model to check that the irreducible gap does not rest on one point.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: The gap should fall with capacity and approach a nonzero floor. It could fail if the 8M model is still improving, which would make the fitted floor unreliable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Width scaling of a routing network trained to its plateau
PROPOSAL: Train transformers of 4M, 16M and 64M parameters on 20-city planar TSP by imitation until validation loss stops moving, then keep training for 3 more rounds, 5 seeds. Report the optimality gap for greedy decoding and for sampling 32 tours, and fit a power law in parameter count. The point is to see whether more capacity still lowers the limit at a size where small models may already be near-optimal.
CONTROLS: The exact-solver length as the lower bound, nearest-neighbour tours as the upper reference, and a refit that drops the 4M model to check that the fitted exponent does not rest on one point.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: The gap should be close to zero for all three sizes and the fit should be flat. It could fail if sampling reveals residual differences that greedy decoding does not show.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Capacity-to-entropy account of the functional form of the gap
PROPOSAL: Test the hypothesis that the optimality gap is governed by the ratio of parameter count to the logarithm of the number of tours. Use trained 2M and 4M parameter transformers on instances with 15, 25 and 35 cities, take the gap at plateau, and regress it on the ratio in log space with 5 seeds. Compare the regression with a linear fit in the city count alone. The prediction is that one line collapses all sizes.
CONTROLS: A shuffled-ratio regression as a null, a fit using parameter count alone, and a fit using city count alone, all scored by held-out error at 45 cities.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: The ratio should explain more variance than either variable alone. It could fail if the two simpler fits do as well, which would leave the mechanism unsupported.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Attention probing as a mechanism study of tour construction
PROPOSAL: Test whether the gap is driven by how attention heads allocate their weight when a tour is built. Train a 32M-parameter transformer on 25-city instances by imitation, record head entropy and the rank of the attended city at 10 checkpoints, and ablate heads in 4 settings, 5 seeds. Compare the change in gap after ablation with the entropy of the ablated head. The prediction is that low-entropy heads matter most.
CONTROLS: A random-head ablation as a null, an ablation of layer norms as a control for generic damage, and a probe on a randomly initialised network of the same architecture.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Ablating low-entropy heads should raise the gap most. It could fail if the damage is similar for all heads, which would leave attention structure unrelated to the limit.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint scaling of city count and point dimension
PROPOSAL: Train a 6M-parameter transformer by imitation on instances with 20, 40 and 80 cities in 2, 4 and 8 dimensions until validation loss stops moving, 8 seeds. Fit the gap with a two-variable power law and test whether the exponents combine multiplicatively. This probes how the solution space and the representation space jointly limit a model of fixed size.
CONTROLS: One-variable fits in city count at 2 dimensions and in dimension at 20 cities as nested alternatives, a nearest-neighbour floor, and a held-out setting of 60 cities in 6 dimensions scored against the fitted surface.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: The joint fit should beat the nested ones on the held-out setting. It could fail if an interaction term is needed, indicating the two limits cannot be separated.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gap scaling for city count and dimension with a deeper network
PROPOSAL: Train a 40M-parameter transformer by imitation on instances with 25 and 50 cities in 2 and 3 dimensions until validation loss stops moving, then fine-tune it with sampling-based rewards for 2 more rounds, 5 seeds. Fit a two-variable power law and test whether the exponents combine multiplicatively. Measure tour length ratio and exact-match rate on 2000 instances.
CONTROLS: One-variable fits in city count at 2 dimensions and in dimension at 25 cities as nested alternatives, a nearest-neighbour floor, a model fine-tuned with shuffled rewards as a control, and a held-out setting of 40 cities in 3 dimensions.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: The joint fit should beat the nested ones on the held-out setting. It could fail if the reward fine-tuning shifts the exponents, in which case the trend would describe the training recipe.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training-length scaling toward the capacity-limited plateau
PROPOSAL: Train a 3M-parameter transformer by imitation on 60-city planar TSP, recording the validation gap after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 epochs of a fixed instance stream, 5 seeds. Fit a saturating power law in epochs, extrapolate the plateau from the first four points, and compare it with the observed gap at 32 epochs. The purpose is to confirm that the plateau used in other experiments really is the limit of the model.
CONTROLS: A fit with the plateau fixed at zero as a naive alternative, a 6M-parameter model to confirm that the plateau moves with model size, and a rerun with a different instance stream to confirm that it does not move with the data.
COST: 144
PREDICTION: The extrapolated plateau should land close to the observed gap at 32 epochs. It could fail if the gap keeps drifting down late in training, which would mean 32 epochs is short of the limit.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dataset size and epoch count for plateau estimation in routing transformers
PROPOSAL: Train a 20M-parameter transformer by imitation on 30-city planar TSP with training sets of 1000, 10000 and 100000 instances, 3 weight decay values, 3 seeds, and record the validation gap at 12 points during training. Fit a saturating power law in epochs and compare the plateau estimates for all the sets. This shows whether data volume changes the plateau at the given capacity. Report the plateau estimates with bootstrap intervals and compare the slope of the fit near its end.
CONTROLS: A fit with the plateau fixed at zero as a naive alternative, a 5M-parameter model to confirm that the plateau moves with capacity, and a rerun with a different instance stream.
COST: 144
PREDICTION: The plateau should be nearly identical for the three sets. It could fail if the 1000-instance set overfits, which would produce a higher plateau for reasons unrelated to capacity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Choosing a performance measure for routing networks near their limit
PROPOSAL: Take 4 trained 3M-parameter checkpoints on 50-city planar TSP and score them with the optimality gap, the fraction of instances within 1 percent of optimal, and the exact-match rate against solver tours on 1000 fresh instances. Fit power laws in checkpoint size for each measure and compare how smoothly each one improves. The aim is to pick a measure that follows predictable trends even without an interpretable loss.
CONTROLS: A reward-style score that counts only optimal tours as a proxy for sparse metrics, bootstrap intervals on every fit, and a held-out set of 100-city instances scored by the same measures.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: The gap and the within-1-percent fraction should improve smoothly while exact match stays near zero. It could fail if all measures are equally smooth, in which case the choice would not matter.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Retraining routing networks to compare smoothness of performance measures
PROPOSAL: Train 3M, 12M and 48M parameter transformers on 50-city planar TSP by imitation and score each with the optimality gap, the fraction of instances within 1 percent of optimal, and the exact-match rate on 1000 fresh instances, 8 seeds. Fit power laws in parameter count for each measure and compare how smoothly each one improves. The aim is to pick a measure that follows predictable trends.
CONTROLS: A reward-style score that counts only optimal tours as a proxy for sparse metrics, bootstrap intervals on every fit, a held-out set of 100-city instances, and a model trained with a smaller batch to test sensitivity.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: The gap and the within-1-percent fraction should improve smoothly while exact match stays near zero. It could fail if the lower learning rate changes the ranking of the measures, which would tie smoothness to the recipe.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Size generalisation far beyond the training range of a routing network
PROPOSAL: Train 10M-parameter transformers by imitation on 20, 30 and 50 cities, then test them zero-shot at 100, 200 and 500 cities and compare with models trained at those sizes by the same procedure, 8 seeds. Fit the gap against city count for both groups and report where the zero-shot trend departs from the trained one. This asks whether simple trends from a limited range survive far outside it.
CONTROLS: Models trained on a mixture of the three training sizes, nearest-neighbour and farthest-insertion floors, and a rescaling of coordinates at test time to check that the departure is not a normalisation artefact.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: The zero-shot gap should rise faster than the trained gap once the size passes about twice the training range. It could fail if the mixture-trained models close the difference, which would put the departure on the data rather than the model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Zero-shot routing at longer instances after training on one size
PROPOSAL: Train 60M-parameter transformers by imitation on 50-city instances only, then test them zero-shot at 100 cities on 1000 instances, with 3 seeds, 3 coordinate normalisations and 2 positional encodings. Compare with models trained at 100 cities by the same procedure. Fit the gap against training step for both groups and report the step at which the zero-shot gap stops falling. Log the entropy of the attention weights at the final step.
CONTROLS: A model trained on a mixture of sizes, nearest-neighbour and farthest-insertion floors, and a rescaling of coordinates at test time, with the positional encodings swapped to learned ones as a control.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: The zero-shot gap should flatten earlier than the trained gap. It could fail if the choice of normalisation moves the plateau, which would make the result depend on preprocessing.
